sections.label: Government securities issuance limit history
sections.summary: The 2021 increase raised the issuance limit from S$690 billion to S$1,065 billion, with S$955 billion outstanding as of end-October 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The last increase to the issuance limit was in 2021, when Parliament authorised the increase of the Government’s issuance limit from S$690 billion to S$1,065 billion, which was intended to last till 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: As of end-October 2024, the outstanding amount of Government securities and T-Bills issued under the GSA is S$955b.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The proposed issuance limit of S$1,515 billion is intended to last till 2029.

sections.label: Proposed GSA issuance ceiling
sections.summary: The Motion proposes raising the ceiling for issuing Government securities and Treasury Bills under the GSA to S$1,515 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For the present Motion, I propose to raise the ceiling for issuing Government securities and Treasury Bills under the GSA to S$1,515 billion.

sections.label: Largest recent limit increase
sections.summary: The increase in the limit is the highest increase over the most recent five instances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, the increase in the limit represents the highest increase over the most recent five instances.

sections.label: Debt-to-GDP burden increase
sections.summary: The $450 billion increase is two-thirds larger than the prior quantum, bringing the total burden to 225% of output.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even so, the present increase calls for $450 billion of an increase, a disproportionately larger two-thirds, relative to the prior quantum.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Between 1992 and 2021, a three-decade period that saw the limit increase six times, the share of debt-to-GDP has always hovered between 110% and 165% of output.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This round will bring the total burden to 225%.

sections.label: Interest repayment burden rise
sections.summary: The interest repayment burden is around three times higher than three years ago.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On balance, the interest repayment burden is around three times higher than what it would have been a mere three years ago.

sections.label: Singapore equity market capitalisation
sections.summary: Singapore's equity market capitalisation has languished relative to other global financial centres, with less global saving reaching the domestic economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The equity market capitalisation share in Singapore has also languished relative to other global financial centres, such as those of stock exchanges in New York, Tokyo, Hong Kong and London.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This means that Singapore has succeeded, certainly, as an international financial centre, but it is more questionable whether it has succeeded as a globally competitive financial market that serves its economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Put another way, as much as we have succeeded in being an intermediary of global saving, less of it appears to have made its way into our domestic economy.

sections.label: SSGS issuance for CPF needs
sections.summary: Over 60% of the increase is expected to be issued as SSGS, mainly to meet CPF's investment needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: More than 60% of the increase is expected to be issued as SSGS, with the primary purpose of meeting CPF's investment needs.

sections.label: Raising borrowing limit approval
sections.summary: The limit will be fully used in 2025, so approval is sought to raise it by $450 billion, estimated to last till 2029.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, our estimate was actually quite accurate, because this time round, the limit will be fully utilised in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, that is why we now are coming back to Parliament to seek approval to raise the limit further, which we estimate, will be sufficient to last us till 2029.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The proposed $450 billion increase is in line with historical trends.
